record.paper_title: Regularity of maximal operators: recent progress and some open problems
record.original_question: Let M be the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on R^d, defined by M f(x) = sup_{r>0} |B(x,r)|^{-1} integral_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy, where B(x,r) is the open ball centered at x with radius r. Let the uncentered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator be defined analogously, except that the supremum is over open balls that contain x and need not be centered at x. For f in W^{1,1}(R^d), is M f weakly differentiable and is the map f -> |grad M f| bounded from W^{1,1}(R^d) to L^1(R^d), equivalently with ||grad M f||_{L^1(R^d)} controlled by C(d)||grad f||_{L^1(R^d)}? Does the same endpoint Sobolev bound hold for the uncentered maximal operator?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let d ≥ 1. For a locally integrable function f : ℝ^d → ℝ, define the centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator by
   (M f)(x) = sup_{r>0} (1/|B(x,r)|) ∫_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy,
where B(x,r) denotes the open Euclidean ball of radius r centered at x, and the uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator by
   (\tilde M f)(x) = sup_{B ∋ x} (1/|B|) ∫_{B} |f(y)| dy,
where the supremum runs over all open Euclidean balls B ⊂ ℝ^d containing x. Let W^{1,1}(ℝ^d) denote the Sobolev space of functions f ∈ L^1(ℝ^d) whose distributional gradient ∇f belongs to L^1(ℝ^d; ℝ^d), equipped with the seminorm ‖∇f‖_{L^1}.

Question: For every f ∈ W^{1,1}(ℝ^d), is M f weakly differentiable, and does there exist a constant C(d) > 0 (depending only on d) such that
   ‖∇ M f‖_{L^1(ℝ^d)} ≤ C(d) ‖∇ f‖_{L^1(ℝ^d)} ?
Equivalently, is the sublinear map f ↦ |∇ M f| bounded from W^{1,1}(ℝ^d) to L^1(ℝ^d)? Does the analogous endpoint bound
   ‖∇ \tilde M f‖_{L^1(ℝ^d)} ≤ C(d) ‖∇ f‖_{L^1(ℝ^d)}
hold for the uncentered maximal operator \tilde M?
artifact.category_tag: Endpoint Sobolev regularity of maximal operators
artifact.status_search_result: The question is the well-known Hajłasz–Onninen endpoint problem. It is settled affirmatively in dimension d = 1 (for both centered and uncentered operators) and for the uncentered operator restricted to radial functions in all dimensions (Luiro), as well as for the centered operator on radial functions (Luiro). The general higher-dimensional case (d ≥ 2) remains open for both centered and uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operators, as documented in recent surveys and ongoing work.

status_evidence.title: Regularity of maximal operators: recent progress and some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Higher dimensional analogues for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, centered or uncentered, are open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The endpoint W^{1,1} bound for the Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator in dimensions d ≥ 2 is open in both centered and uncentered cases.

status_evidence.title: Endpoint Sobolev Bounds for Fractional Hardy-Littlewood Maximal Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work establishes endpoint Sobolev bounds for fractional maximal operators, but the non-fractional case in higher dimensions remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Progress exists for fractional analogues; the original non-fractional question in d ≥ 2 is still open.
